method_note: Targeting Argo CD v3.4.x (GA; latest stable v3.4.3, May 2026) and the v3.3.x maintenance line. Test prompts are realistic flavor — informal punctuation, abbreviated context. Skill should produce production-ready YAML with v3.x defaults baked in (annotation tracking, ServerSideApply, RespectIgnoreDifferences=true, no `default` project).

evals.name: applicationset-helm-oci-per-dir
evals.prompt: set up a new ApplicationSet that creates one Argo CD app per directory under apps/staging/ in our config repo at github.com/example/cluster-config (revision main). Each app should deploy a helm chart from oci://my-registry.example.com/charts and override values from a values.yaml in the same directory. We use kubernetes the destination is in-cluster and the namespace should match the directory name. We're on argo cd v3.3.9. give me the manifest plus a short note on the gotchas
evals.expected_output: ApplicationSet YAML using Git directories generator, goTemplate: true, goTemplateOptions: [missingkey=error], OCI Helm chart source pinned by digest (or at least tag), correct destination, hard-coded project (not templated), with a note on the goTemplate=false default trap, the v3.0+ annotation-tracking default, ApplicationSet finalizer placement, OCI digest pinning best practice, and ServerSideApply syncOption recommendation. Should NOT recommend `path: dir/**` (doesn't recurse).
assertions: The manifest uses an ApplicationSet with a Git generator that enumerates directories under apps/staging/ using a single-level glob such as apps/staging/*, and does not use a `**` recursive glob pattern
The ApplicationSet sets goTemplate to true and sets goTemplateOptions to include missingkey=error
The project field in the generated Application template is a fixed literal value rather than a value derived from generator variables such as the directory path or basename

The generated Applications pull the Helm chart from the oci://my-registry.example.com/charts registry and override values with the per-directory values.yaml, with the destination namespace derived from the directory name
The answer specifies a pinned chart version reference (a digest or explicit chart version/tag) rather than leaving the OCI chart reference floating or unversioned
The resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io finalizer, if present, is placed in the Application template metadata rather than only on the ApplicationSet's own metadata
The answer flags at least one behavioral trap that would silently produce wrong results, such as the legacy non-Go templating default or v3.x annotation-based resource tracking

evals.name: outofsync-hpa-replicas
evals.prompt: my Application is stuck OutOfSync — kubectl shows the Deployment exists and the spec matches what's in git, but argo cd says replicas differ. I have an HPA on it. how do I make argo stop fighting the HPA? we're on 3.3
evals.expected_output: Should diagnose: HPA mutates Deployment.spec.replicas; without ignoreDifferences + RespectIgnoreDifferences=true the controller will sync-loop. Provides the exact ignoreDifferences entry (group: apps, kind: Deployment, jsonPointers: [/spec/replicas]) plus RespectIgnoreDifferences=true syncOption. May also suggest removing replicas from the Deployment template entirely (Argo's best_practices.md recommendation) or using ServerSideDiff=true. Should NOT suggest disabling selfHeal as the primary fix (cruder). Should NOT suggest IncludeMutationWebhook=true (that annotation is the CVE-2026-42880 vector and removed/dangerous).
assertions: The answer identifies the HPA writing to the Deployment's spec.replicas field as the cause of the persistent OutOfSync state
The answer supplies an ignoreDifferences entry scoped to group apps, kind Deployment, targeting the /spec/replicas field

The answer states that the ignoreDifferences entry alone is insufficient for the apply path and pairs it with the RespectIgnoreDifferences=true sync option (or an equivalent server-side diff mechanism)
The answer does NOT present turning off selfHeal (or disabling automated sync) as the primary recommended fix
The answer does NOT recommend the IncludeMutationWebhook=true compare-option
Any suggestion to remove the replicas field from the Deployment manifest in git is presented as a valid fix or complement rather than being contradicted

evals.name: presync-db-migration-hook
evals.prompt: I need a presync hook that runs db migrations before each deploy. The migration is a Job. it must complete before the app rolls forward, and we want old completed jobs cleaned up but kept on failure for debugging. show me the right manifest
evals.expected_output: Job with argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync and argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy: HookSucceeded (succeeded jobs cleaned up, failed jobs kept for debugging). Should use `metadata.generateName` (NOT a fixed name) to avoid the 'PreSync hook re-run' issue. Optionally a Sync wave on the Job. Brief explanation of phase ordering: PreSync runs before Sync; if hook fails, app goes Failed and Sync doesn't proceed. Should NOT use BeforeHookCreation policy with a generateName job (that pairing leaks Jobs across syncs).
assertions: The Job carries the hook annotation designating it as a PreSync hook
The hook delete policy is set so that successful hook runs are garbage-collected while failed runs are retained for inspection
The Job uses generateName rather than a fixed metadata.name
The answer does NOT set BeforeHookCreation as the delete policy on this Job
The answer states that the PreSync hook must reach completion before the main sync phase applies workloads, and that a hook failure aborts the sync

evals.name: appproject-multitenant-with-impersonation
evals.prompt: we're a platform team setting up multi-tenant argo cd. team-payments needs their own AppProject that can only sync to namespaces starting with `payments-`, only from our company gitlab repos under `gitlab.example.com/payments/`, and we want their syncs to use a per-app ServiceAccount so kubernetes RBAC limits the blast radius. write the AppProject. We're on argo cd v3.4 RC.
evals.expected_output: AppProject with: namespace argocd, finalizer resources-finalizer.argocd.argoproj.io, sourceRepos: ['https://gitlab.example.com/payments/*'], destinations with namespace: 'payments-*' glob, an explicit clusterResourceWhitelist that's tight (Namespace + minimal cluster resources, NOT '*'), namespaceResourceBlacklist for Secret (or note that ESO/SealedSecrets is recommended), AND destinationServiceAccounts block (sync impersonation, Beta in v3.4). Should mention: impersonation is keyed by `server` not `name` so destinations should standardize on server URL; the SA needs perms for both apply ops AND server ops (logs/exec) in v3.4. Should NOT use spec.project: default. May add signatureKeys for signed-commit enforcement.
assertions: The AppProject restricts sourceRepos to a pattern scoped to gitlab.example.com/payments/ rather than allowing all repositories
The destinations entry limits the namespace to a payments- prefixed glob rather than allowing all namespaces
The clusterResourceWhitelist is an explicit enumerated list rather than a wildcard permitting all cluster-scoped kinds
The manifest includes a destinationServiceAccounts configuration mapping destinations to per-app ServiceAccounts for sync impersonation
The answer does NOT assign the tenant to the built-in default project or otherwise leave the tenant's apps on an unrestricted project

The answer notes a concrete operational constraint of impersonation, such as destination matching being keyed on the cluster server URL rather than the cluster name, or the ServiceAccount needing permissions beyond plain apply
The answer restricts or explicitly addresses tenant handling of Secret resources (blacklisting the kind or directing them to an external secrets mechanism)

evals.name: upgrade-3.1-to-3.3-app-author-perspective
evals.prompt: upgrading from argo cd 3.1 to 3.3, what app-author-facing changes do I need to know about? what should I update in our manifests?
evals.expected_output: Should call out: (1) v3.3 SSA migration regression — skip 3.3.0/3.3.1, upgrade direct to 3.3.2+; ApplicationSet CRD exceeds client-side-apply 256KB annotation limit so use server-side apply; if Argo manages itself, set ServerSideApply=true on the meta-app. (2) `automated.enabled: true|false` field added in 3.1 — use to pause apps cleanly. (3) `Prune=confirm`/`Delete=confirm` per-resource annotations added in 3.3. (4) PreDelete/PostDelete hooks added in 3.3. (5) `SkipDryRunOnMissingResource=true` syncOption added in 3.1. (6) clusterResourceWhitelist now scopable by name (3.3). (7) Maturity: Server-Side Diff stable since 3.2; Progressive Sync formal Beta in 3.3; OCI source Beta since 3.1. (8) CVE-2026-42880 patched in 3.3.8+ — strip IncludeMutationWebhook=true. (9) Hydrator state moved to git-notes in 3.3 (relevant only if using Source Hydrator). Should NOT mention v3.4 features. Should reference upgrade docs path.
assertions: The answer warns that the 3.3.0 and 3.3.1 releases contain a server-side-apply migration defect and directs the upgrade to 3.3.2 or later
The answer states that a self-managing Argo CD Application needs ServerSideApply enabled because the ApplicationSet CRD exceeds the client-side apply annotation size limit
The answer identifies the automated.enabled boolean as the supported way to pause automated sync rather than deleting the automated block
The answer identifies confirmation-gated prune/delete for destructive resources as newly available in this version range

The answer identifies at least two additional app-author-facing additions in the 3.1-3.3 window (e.g. PreDelete/PostDelete hooks, SkipDryRunOnMissingResource, name-scoped clusterResourceWhitelist, Server-Side Diff reaching stable, Progressive Sync at Beta, OCI sources at Beta)
The answer instructs removing IncludeMutationWebhook=true from manifests and ties it to a security advisory fixed within the 3.3 line
The answer does NOT attribute features introduced in v3.4 or later to this 3.1-to-3.3 upgrade

evals.name: multisource-oci-chart-git-values
evals.prompt: We're on Argo CD 3.4.5. I need to write the Application for kube-prometheus-stack. The chart is mirrored into our Harbor at oci://harbor.example.com/charts/kube-prometheus-stack, currently version 78.2.1. The values files are NOT in the chart — they live in our config repo github.com/example/cluster-config (branch main) under values/observability/base.yaml and values/observability/prod.yaml, and they change far more often than the chart does. Target is the cluster registered as prod-eu-1, namespace monitoring (which doesn't exist yet), AppProject is observability. Automated sync with prune and self-heal is fine, nothing mutates these specs. One hard requirement from our security team: if somebody re-pushes the 78.2.1 tag in Harbor, our cluster must not silently pick up different content. Give me the full manifest.
evals.expected_output: A single multi-source Application where the git repo is declared as a ref-only source and the OCI chart source pulls its valueFiles through that ref, so values can change without touching the chart. The chart must be pinned by digest (not just the mutable 78.2.1 tag) to satisfy the re-tag requirement, and the manifest must handle kube-prometheus-stack's oversized CRDs so the first sync doesn't fail.
assertions: The manifest uses a single Application with multiple sources where the Helm chart consumes valueFiles from the separate git repo via a source reference, rather than copying values into the chart repo or splitting this into two Applications
The git repo source is declared as a values-only/reference source that does not itself render manifests into the cluster
The OCI chart is pinned to an immutable digest, or the answer explicitly states that the 78.2.1 tag is mutable in Harbor and shows the digest-pinned form that satisfies the security requirement

The manifest handles kube-prometheus-stack's very large CRDs so the sync does not fail on the client-side-apply annotation size limit (e.g. server-side apply, Replace, or skipping CRDs with a stated alternative for installing them)
Destination targets cluster prod-eu-1 and namespace monitoring, the namespace gets created by the sync, and the project is observability rather than default

Automated sync is enabled with prune and self-heal, and the manifest is internally consistent (no mixing of a single-source field with the multi-source list, ref alias in valueFiles matches the declared ref)

evals.name: prune-ignores-preupgrade-resources
evals.prompt: Weird one. We removed the redis-cache StatefulSet, its Service and its PDB from git about six weeks ago (deleted the files, PR merged). The Application `checkout-api` says Synced and Healthy, `prune: true` and `selfHeal: true` are both set in syncPolicy.automated, but all three objects are still running in the cluster. `argocd app diff checkout-api` shows nothing. What's stranger: we deleted a ConfigMap from the same app last week and that one got pruned within a minute. The only thing I can think of that's different is that the redis objects were first created back when we were on Argo CD 2.13 — we went 2.13 → 3.0 → 3.4.5 last November. Everything created since the upgrade prunes fine. I've already tried a hard refresh and a manual `argocd app sync --prune`; neither touched them. What's going on and how do I clean this up without nuking things I actually need?
evals.expected_output: The answer identifies that the leftover objects still carry only the pre-v3 label-based ownership marker and lack the annotation-based tracking id that v3.x uses by default, so the controller no longer considers them part of the Application — which is why the app reports Synced, the diff is empty, and prune never touches them. It should explain how to find every other object in the same state and give a safe remediation.
assertions: Identifies the ownership/resource-tracking metadata mismatch on objects created before the v3 upgrade (label-based marker vs the annotation the current version expects) as the root cause

Explicitly rules out the obvious suspects the user already checked — prune being disabled, syncPolicy misconfiguration, or a stale cache — and explains why the app correctly reports Synced despite the objects existing
Explains that these objects are now unowned/orphaned from Argo CD's perspective, so no amount of refresh, re-sync or prune will remove them while they stay untracked

Gives a concrete way to discover the other objects across apps that are in the same untracked state (e.g. orphaned-resource surfacing or querying for the legacy marker without the current tracking metadata) rather than only fixing these three

Proposes a remediation that either re-establishes Argo CD ownership before pruning or removes the leftovers directly, and does not advise deleting the whole namespace, the Application, or every object carrying the legacy label without first confirming which are genuinely orphaned

evals.name: mutation-webhook-compare-option-cve
evals.prompt: Our Kyverno mutating webhook injects resource limits and a couple of labels into every Deployment, and Istio injects the sidecar. Result: apps flip to OutOfSync seconds after a successful sync and self-heal keeps re-syncing them. I found that ServerSideDiff plus the `argocd.argoproj.io/compare-options: IncludeMutationWebhook=true` annotation makes Argo CD account for the webhook output so the diff comes out clean. We're running Argo CD 3.3.6. I want to roll this out to all ~60 apps at once by putting it in the metadata.annotations of our ApplicationSet template — the same AppSet also generates apps that manage External Secrets-created Secrets. About 40 developers have read access to applications in the Argo UI. Give me the exact annotation block to drop into the template.
evals.expected_output: A correct answer refuses to roll the annotation out on 3.3.6, because on that build enabling the mutation-webhook compare option exposes plaintext Secret data to every principal with application read access — here, 40 developers. It should name the patched version floor for the 3.3 line, and give a working alternative for suppressing the webhook-induced OutOfSync that doesn't require the vulnerable option.
assertions: Does NOT hand over the annotation as a safe change to apply on 3.3.6, and does not recommend rolling it into the ApplicationSet template on the current build

States that on their running version this option leaks plaintext Secret contents to anyone holding application read permission, and connects that directly to the 40 developers with UI read access and the External Secrets-managed Secrets
Names a concrete patched version floor in the 3.3 line (3.3.9 or later) that must be reached before the option is usable, rather than only saying 'upgrade'

Provides a workable alternative that stops the webhook-driven OutOfSync flapping without the vulnerable option — e.g. targeted ignoreDifferences on the injected fields (with the sync option that makes them respected on apply) or managed-fields-manager based ignores — concrete enough to act on
Does NOT propose disabling self-heal or automated sync fleet-wide as the remedy for the flapping
Recommends preventing the value from reappearing (CI/policy check or equivalent) rather than relying on the team to remember
